key_insight: SeqSmoother uses transformer-based temporal correction plus physics-informed spectral cues to estimate sleep heart rate from wrist accelerometry without requiring optical sensors.
engineering_relevance: This enables population-scale cardiac monitoring from accelerometer-rich cohorts where ECG/PPG are unavailable, while highlighting the trade-off between broader coverage and per-window accuracy.
method: Transformer-based temporal smoother for sleep HR estimation
Combines spectral descriptors with a Nightbeat-derived frequency anchor
Adds a sub-harmonic feature to detect harmonic lock-on failures
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 13 participant-disjoint held-out folds with matched 60-s windows and 15-s steps; SeqSmoother reached 1.60 bpm macro MAE, while Nightbeat was more accurate on retained matched intervals but covered only 72.85% as many eligible out-of-fold estimates.
watch_item: Performance depends on label quality and quality-gated intervals, so deployment must handle missing estimates and possible harmonic frequency lock-on failures.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Sleep Heart Rate Estimation from Accelerometers: Toward Population-Scale Cardiac Insight Without Optical Sensors
